observation.visible_scene: A wide beach at sunset (or sunrise). The upper two-thirds of the frame is a sky filled with streaked clouds lit in orange, yellow, pink and purple on the left and teal-blue on the right, with the sun a bright low glow near the horizon at center-right. Below the horizon is the sea, marked by a long horizontal band of breaking white foam in the middle distance. The foreground is flat, wet, mirror-like sand that reflects the sky: warm golden-orange on the left and cool cyan-teal on the right, with a thin curved water edge line running across it.
visible_changes: The surf band in the middle distance continuously reshapes: its white foam crest thickens, thins and shifts in texture from frame to frame, indicating an ongoing wave breaking along the line rather than a single event.
The thin water edge on the wet foreground sand creeps slightly forward and back across the clip, so the boundary between the dark reflective sand and the shallow wash moves by a small amount.
The colored reflections on the wet sand shimmer and subtly change shape as the shallow water moves, but the overall orange-left / teal-right reflection pattern persists.
The cloud formations, the sun's position on the horizon, and the horizon line remain essentially fixed throughout the excerpt (no visible drift).
The camera viewpoint is static; the only motion is the water (waves, foam and shoreline wash).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the wave line is on an advancing or receding part of a longer swell cycle, and the tide trend beyond this short window.
What happens to the wave set before the first frame and after the last frame, since both ends are arbitrary crops of continuous surf.
uncertain_details: The exact vertical position of the breaking-wave crest changes only marginally, so any net advance or retreat of the wave line is hard to confirm versus mere foam-texture change.
Subtle apparent shifts in the foreground water edge could be partly reflection/water movement rather than a true translation of the shoreline.
